resolvedNearCopies.newDemand: Remove a repeated subject after a relative clause

skillProofs.activityRationale: Instruments is the subject and recorded is a finite verb. While makes that complete subject-verb clause dependent on another statement.

Bowl needs a finite main verb. Was displayed supplies it; displaying is nonfinite and which was displayed creates another modifying clause. The participle decorated does not supply the main predicate.
Unless introduces a dependent condition. A comma attaches it to the main clause beginning the engineer; a semicolon cannot follow the dependent clause, and a period strands it as a fragment.

Each side has its own subject and verb. Comma plus so supplies a correct coordinating boundary and the result relationship; however between commas still creates a splice, and so, puts the comma on the wrong side.

The survey was short and every response required a detailed explanation are independent clauses. However is a conjunctive adverb, so a semicolon or period belongs before it; neither a comma alone nor and however supplies the offered standard construction.

The core sentence is “The guidelines specify the minimum training.” Guidelines is plural, so specify supplies its main verb. The which-clause adds information about the revision, and each volunteer must complete describes training. Neither supplies a main verb for guidelines. Specifying cannot complete the main sentence alone; that specify begins another dependent clause.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The team kept the marks because they preserved evidence of the repair.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Because makes the evidence the motive for preservation. Although would present that evidence as an obstacle; the semicolon cannot introduce the dependent because-clause.

The name identifies one of several guides, so it stays attached without commas. Paired commas would treat it as added information about someone already identified; a single trailing comma splits the subject from its verb.

After makes the opening clause dependent, so a comma separates it from the following main clause. A semicolon would treat it as independent; omitting the comma obscures the boundary after the introductory clause.
The photograph remained is the main clause. The optional description taken at dawn requires both opening and closing commas; either single-comma alternative leaves an unbalanced interruption.

White identifies the color of the cotton coat, and clean describes that combined phrase. These cumulative modifiers do not form a simple coordinate list; neither a comma nor a semicolon belongs at the blank.
When a state follows a city inside a sentence, set it off with commas on both sides: Albany, New York, before opening. Either one-sided option leaves the state only partly set off.
The that-clause identifies the ten affected folders. It is part of the subject, so no mark separates that full subject from were moved. A comma or semicolon would break the subject-verb connection.
The opening dash introduces an added description. A matching dash closes it before has finally been attributed, the painting’s main predicate. A comma or colon would not match the opening delimiter.
The that-clause identifies the parcels and remains inside the subject. No mark separates that full subject from are waiting; a comma or semicolon would break the subject-verb connection.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: It identifies the capsule as the owner without a contraction.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Its is the possessive pronoun showing whose outer layer dried. It does not expand to it is and does not form a plural. In a drill, expanding an apostrophe form is a useful way to test the competing contraction.
More than one researcher owns the containers, so use the regular plural researchers followed by an apostrophe. Researcher’s is singular possession; researchers alone is a plain plural.

A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark when the reporting phrase continues the same sentence: sealed,” the supervisor said. The period would incorrectly end the quotation before the lower-case reporting tag; a semicolon does not attach that tag.

Comma plus so coordinates the independent clauses and states the result. Therefore is an adverb rather than a coordinating conjunction, so the comma alternative with therefore and the comma alone both create splices.

The emergency kit contained the following items is a complete clause. A colon introduces the list explaining those items. A semicolon would need a complete following clause; a comma alone does not perform the offered list-introduction job.

The comma after manuscript opens a nonessential which-clause. A second comma must close it before contains, the main verb. A dash would mismatch the opener; a semicolon cannot divide this subject from its predicate.

A dash can introduce the phrase identifying the one open route. The footpath phrase is not an independent clause for a semicolon, and comma plus and would wrongly try to coordinate it with a complete clause.

Each whole item contains a name and an appositive role, so semicolons separate the items without confusing those boundaries with internal commas. The final semicolon may precede and because it separates list items rather than clauses.

The introduction is a complete clause, and the following complete clause identifies its solution, so a colon introduces the elaboration. A comma would splice the clauses; semicolon plus because would strand a dependent clause.
Condition is the singular head subject; shelves and windows are embedded in modifying phrases. Concerns agrees with condition, while concern and have concerned are plural forms.
Every one is the singular subject. Crates belongs to an of-phrase and label is the object, so neither controls the verb. This subject check can then guide verb-form choices in other sentences.
Inspected and tightened establish a completed past-tense sequence, so closed continues it. Closing has no finite auxiliary; closes introduces an unjustified present-tense shift.
Put is the past participle as well as the simple past of put, so had put is correct. Putting would need been after had; puts is a present form and cannot follow had.
The nearer subject is singular manager, so has agrees. Inspectors is farther from the verb and does not control this neither/nor construction.
The guide reclined and placed no object, so the past tense of lie is lay. Laid is the past of lay meaning place an object; lain is a participle that needs a form of have.
The subject after the verb is singular machine, not cabinets. Stands agrees with machine; stand and have stood are plural.
Still and today identify an ongoing present condition, so sways fits. The earlier recorded belongs to 1974 and does not force the next sentence into the past.
Invited takes an object: invited me. Adding Suri and does not change the required case. I is a subject form; myself has no matching first-person subject to reflect back to.
The board selects him or her, so whomever fills the object position inside the clause. Whoever is a subject form; whose is possessive. The pronoun’s own clause determines case.
The board owns the revised plan. Managers and office are nearby nouns, but they do not supply the intended owner; identify the antecedent before choosing a possessive form in a new sentence.
The trophy states the intended referent. This object could still name either nearby object, and the vase changes the intended event.

The main sentence is “The pilot will testify tomorrow.” Within the relative clause, who is the subject of reported: “she reported the fault.” The investigators believe reports that claim; it does not turn who into an object. Whom is an object form, and whose is possessive.
The telescope, not the nearby students, owns the cover. Its supplies singular possession; their points to a plural owner, and it’s is a contraction.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: the astronomer prepared a list of targets
skillProofs.activityRationale: The astronomer can be eager and is the subject of the keyed clause. A list and the act of preparing cannot feel eager, so those choices dangle the opening modifier.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The engineer sent a diagram printed on recycled paper to the client.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Printed on recycled paper must describe diagram, so it belongs beside diagram. The other placements make client the object printed or garble the intended relationship.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The guide accepted donations only from adults.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Only from adults limits the group allowed to donate. Only accepted can limit the action; only donations limits the things accepted. The surrounding sentence requires a distinction between the donors and the people whose questions were answered.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: the stones were stored in separate boxes
skillProofs.activityRationale: The stones were weighed and photographed; the keyed passive clause keeps stones as its subject. The field team and the activity of storing do not name the objects receiving the opening actions.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Readers may view the letters only after orientation.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Only after orientation restricts the condition or time of viewing. Only readers restricts who may view; only the letters restricts what they may view. Neither expresses the stated timing requirement.
Informative and accessible are adjectives describing exhibition, so engaging matches their role. A complete clause and a prepositional phrase do not continue the adjective series.
Editing and playing are gerunds naming the two activities. To play changes the established form; when we played gives a time clause rather than the corresponding activity.

How to can govern both measure angles and measure distances. Measuring changes to a gerund; they measure introduces a complete clause. Optional repeated wording is not required when the construction is shared.
Either joins complete the online module with attend the workshop, both verb phrases governed by must. A passive clause and a gerund do not match that construction.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: to publish a complete condition report
skillProofs.activityRationale: To insure and to publish are parallel infinitive requirements imposed on the museum. A noun phrase and a that-clause do not continue the same paired construction.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: how accurately they documented the sources
skillProofs.activityRationale: The first two criteria ask how well something was done. How accurately continues that structure; whether asks a yes/no question, and their sources merely names a thing.

A compliment is praise, while complement means suit or complete something. The sentence says the reviewer praised a color scheme that would go well with the exhibits, so the second pair fits both roles.
Rather pairs with than to compare check with guess. Then marks sequence, not preference; as does not complete the rather...than construction.
Might requires have before the participle delivered in this construction. Of imitates the sound of might’ve but is not a verb; might had is not a valid auxiliary sequence.
Waste is treated as a mass, so less applies. Containers are separate countable objects, so fewer applies. The other pairs attach count forms to mass nouns or mass forms to count nouns.
Preferable pairs with to when comparing two options. Than is used after comparative forms such as better, but not in preferable to; from does not fit the construction.
That of the old cabinet means the height of the old cabinet. The other choices compare a height with an entire object or the activity of building it.
Looked means appeared here, so the adjective pale describes ink. Palely is an adverb and paleness is a noun. Evenly correctly describes the action applied in the second clause.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: It selected the cheapest of the five plans.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Cheapest is the superlative selecting the minimum within a set of five. Cheaper is comparative, and most cheapest doubles the superlative marking.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The key was found during renovation.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The passive sentence keeps the key as the subject and states only the known discovery. The other choices invent a discoverer or change finding into deliberate concealment. Passive voice can be the most accurate choice.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Yes, because it supplies another consequence supporting the repair.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The sentence adds a distinct consequence, reduced pressure at a relevant public facility, which supports the repair argument. It does not repeat a quantity or explain the repair procedure; both verdict and reason must be true.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: No, because the biographical detail interrupts the focusing procedure.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The local purpose is to explain a procedure. The biography does not supply a step, so it should be omitted here. It does not contradict the procedure, and a shared topic alone does not establish relevance.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The same energy-use comparison in different words
skillProofs.activityRationale: Half as much and fifty percent lower express the same comparison. The sentence adds neither a cause nor a maintenance requirement, so keeping it would repeat information rather than develop the paragraph.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: It anticipates why the website alone would not meet those readers’ needs.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The lack of access explains why later readers still need a way to locate materials during library visits. It neither establishes universal accuracy nor repeats the website launch; it supplies needed background for the argument.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: No, because it does not explain either the box’s mechanism or the readings.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The award concerns the manufacturer but supplies no evidence about insulation and no definition of the mechanism. It interrupts the link between the explanation and its measured result.

Before beginning requires the setting to be adjusted before measurement starts. After sentence 1 supplies the connected recorder and precedes sentence 2; the later positions adjust it only after data collection has begun or ended.

That flaw refers to the leak in sentence 1 and interprets its significance before sentence 2 describes the repair. The later positions separate the explanation from the finding and report the response before its reasoning.

These discoveries refers to finding the signs in sentence 1. Immediately afterward it explains that discovery’s significance before the paragraph moves to the future display; earlier it lacks a referent, and later it interrupts the shift to plans.
Sentences 1–2 explain the mechanism; sentence 3 introduces cost, developed in sentence 4. The other breaks divide the explanation or separate the new cost claim from its support.

After A the sentence interprets the visibility/overheating tradeoff, then prepares the change in B. Before A it lacks the established problem; after B it no longer explains the decision before that decision is introduced.

The proposal must precede the objection; that objection in A points back to B. The tested response then leads to the adoption in D. The other orders either introduce criticism before the proposal or respond before the criticism appears.
Receive already conveys taking something in. The first option repeats incoming and coming in; the last repeats the verb’s meaning. The sentence already supplies the object signals after the blank.
Because directly states the reason the lab delayed opening. The other phrases express the same cause with more words and no useful added meaning.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: OMIT both commas and the inserted phrase
skillProofs.activityRationale: The main sentence needs no personal aside: The engineer tested the emergency lights before signing the report. The other choices add unrelated background and disrupt the inspection’s focus.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Thirty-two of the forty volunteers reported that the labels were easier to read.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The keyed summary keeps both the volunteer sample and the self-reported outcome. The other choices generalize to visitors or people beyond the sample and replace a reported opinion with demonstrated reading improvement.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Reading rooms provide adjustable lamps for examining faint handwriting.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The first choice adds a practical detail about working in the reading room. The other two express the opening appointment rule again in different words.
Instead marks the contrast between the expected short repair and the actual long closure. The second statement is not an example of a weekend repair or a similar outcome.
The ferry deliveries result from the bridge closure, so Consequently expresses cause and effect. They are neither an example of an inspection nor a parallel event.
While introduces the simultaneous warming interval. Afterward would put preparation later; Therefore would claim the warming caused the preparation instead of locating it in time.
Noise reduction is another benefit rather than a restatement of heat loss or a contrast with it. Moreover adds that independent supporting point.
In fact introduces the actual use in correction of the visitors’ assumption. Grain storage is not an example of a watchpost or a similar use.

Nevertheless concedes accuracy and ease of use, then introduces the independent parts problem that blocked purchase. The favorable evidence did not cause postponement, and postponement does not restate it.
The tactile models supply another way of improving access, so In addition fits. They do not restate the height change, and they do not reverse it.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: She checked each stitch under magnification before moving to the next.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Inspecting every stitch under magnification demonstrates careful work through a concrete action. The room size and opening time concern the setting rather than the quality the question asks to emphasize.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The volunteers’ shared effort kept the river crossing open.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The shared effort conclusion synthesizes the fuel, repairs, and shifts. The other details may concern ferries or the river but do not conclude the paragraph’s explanation of how the service survived.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Dust settled where the ticket window had once glowed on winter evenings.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The subdued image of dust replacing the lit ticket window supports quiet regret. The shopping proposal changes to optimism about redevelopment; the final choice uses slang that clashes with the reflective tone.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The route still served all twelve stops, and average travel time fell by nine minutes.
skillProofs.activityRationale: All twelve stops supports unchanged access, and a nine-minute reduction supports shorter journeys. The other choices give satisfaction or ridership evidence without establishing both requested outcomes.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The card’s empty lines now held all our handwriting, and my cousin reached for the pen.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Shared handwriting and the cousin reaching for the pen develop the unfinished recipe image into ongoing family transmission. The other choices offer ingredients or storage advice without completing the essay’s meaning.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Missed appointments fell, while patients’ average fares remained unchanged.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Fewer missed appointments supports attendance; unchanged fares supports the travel-cost limit. Facilities, staffing, and hours are relevant to a clinic but do not establish the two outcomes in the claim.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Yes, because the damage and the explanation of vulnerability motivate the later changes.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The essay connects the problem and its cause to the revised storage, which meets the specified explanatory goal. An architectural history is unnecessary, and the text does not compare literary styles.

Historic means historically important, matching the lasting change. Noticeable concerns how easily something attracts attention, which the first clause limits; noisy describes sound rather than significance.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: A compromise involves concessions; a consensus is general agreement.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Compromise describes reaching an agreement through concessions, while consensus means general agreement and need not involve concessions. The other statements reverse or erase those distinctions.
Raise takes questions as an object, and advice is the noun for guidance. Rise does not take that object, while advise is the verb rather than the noun required after final.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The change reduced average processing time.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Reduced average processing time states a precise, measured result. Crushed and way less annoying add colloquial intensity or an unsupported reaction instead of maintaining the report’s register.
An allusion is an indirect reference; the reader infers the connection from evidence. An illusion is a false impression, imply describes the act of suggesting, and elude means escape.

Disinterested means impartial in judgment; credible describes claims that are believable. Uninterested means not interested, credulous describes an overly trusting person, and the final pair does not express the stated distinctions.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Nobody else in the group could ever do work as good as mine.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The first statement claims superiority over everyone else without support. Thanking a teammate and acknowledging remaining flaws are consistent with justified satisfaction rather than excessive self-regard.

The expression is focuses on: focuses governs the preposition introducing the subject of attention. Course names what does the focusing, and damage belongs to the later -ing phrase rather than determining this preposition.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The reported pattern occurred in the studied village; a wider pattern has not yet been established.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The middle choice preserves the stated observation and the limit on generalization. Studying one place does not prove the result everywhere, but limited scope does not make the reported observation false.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The condition for issuing the permit has not been met.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Contingent on makes a satisfactory inspection a prerequisite. A defect means the stated requirement has not been satisfied; it does not guarantee the permit or make the inspection irrelevant.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: The sentence loses its main verb and becomes a fragment.
skillProofs.activityRationale: Provides is the main verb for entrance. Opened belongs to the embedded which-clause and cannot replace it, so deletion leaves a fragment. A shorter answer is useful only if required structure survives.
Ending at layers keeps the measured finding and the formal register. The other choices retain a conversational reaction that the report does not need.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: copper and tin salvaged from the old shipyard
skillProofs.activityRationale: Copper and tin names the materials, and the old shipyard supplies their source. The first names neither; the last names the materials but substitutes a time requirement for their source.
Faded directly modifies photographs in the keyed phrase. The other versions attach it to the guide or harbor rather than the photographs.
Preoccupied with introduces what holds attention; capable of takes the following -ing form. The other preposition pairs do not fit those constructions.

But coordinates the clauses and states the contrast between extra distance and avoiding flooding. Therefore between commas creates a splice and implies the wrong consequence; and, adds an unnecessary comma.

Made one point: it yields a complete introduction followed by its explanation. The second option repeats showed from outside the underline; the third puts a dependent because-clause after a semicolon.

skillProofs.activityAnswer: Forty-eight volunteers reported that the map was easier to follow.
skillProofs.activityRationale: The keyed choice retains both the sample and the self-reported measure. The other statements generalize to everyone or claim timed/accuracy outcomes that the study did not test.
